planning for queues that share agents, agent scripts on the desk, one-click fixes from the centre summary, the Partner Academy for dealers and resellers, and the Imara CX edition's Marketing Manager and demo calls.

Workforce, planning ahead: plan queues that share agents without counting anyone twice, on Today, Plan and Build schedule. A long-term people plan shows how many agents you need month by month, and outbound campaigns get their own forecast and a campaign view on Today. New reports close out the workforce programme.

Workforce, rounds and wait lists: run shift-choice and time-off rounds, where agents pick in turn and the award keeps cover, balance and limits. When a day is full, time off goes on a wait list and is offered when a place opens; unused leave can carry over. Find a time suggests a slot for meetings and training when the people needed are free.

Workforce, smaller changes: the Adherence page has a conformance column, the agent panel on the schedule week shows the agent's availability, and leave that is approved automatically tells team leaders for information only.

Agent scripts on the desk: agents follow a script step by step during a call, with branches, and can go back a step. A script step can send an email or SMS, or start a DebiCheck mandate, with the same checks as a journey (do-not-contact lists, a verified caller, the client's own messaging account). The AI scores how well a script was followed into QA, and a Script adherence report shows it per agent and script. The help guide and Academy lessons cover the Scripts page and the desk.

Field privacy in scripts: details hidden from an agent stay hidden in what a script sends, in ticket threads, customer history, transcripts, the call library, QA and AI summaries. The script designer warns when an email subject would carry a hidden field.

Centre summary, one-click fixes: when the centre summary suggests a fix, such as a slower dialler pace or a ticket setting, a supervisor can apply it with one click, see it marked Applied in the summary PDF and the morning health email, and undo it.

Partner Academy: dealers and resellers learn the platform on the Academy's own screens, in a Sales and a Technical track with lessons, walkthrough videos with captions, and explainers for call paths and rate cards. An exam gives a certificate for 12 months, with a public page to check it. Update add-ons keep a certificate current, with 30 days' grace and reminders. Learners can open a practice organisation to try things safely; it cannot order, port or be given real numbers and is removed after 14 days. A platform operator can require a current certificate before a partner creates organisations or carriers. Operators manage it all from a new Partner Academy item in the Platform menu.

Imara CX edition: a Marketing Manager that plans and sends an organisation's marketing within a set budget, with weekly reports and a nudge on WhatsApp to rescue a trial that has gone quiet; a website demo call, where a visitor talks to a real AI caller; usage prices and marketing settings on screen; and suspended organisations kept on hold for 90 days before deletion. These switch on only for Imara and change nothing for existing organisations.

Fixes: sandbox organisations cannot order or port numbers; the ticket apps panel shows an empty list instead of an error when apps are not set up; the tickets list keeps the latest resolved tickets and always has a sort; late-reply alerts name the ticket that is still open, not an older closed one."}
